channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Proposed constitutional amendments fail to gain ballot access
item.description: An amendment aimed at expanding Medicaid coverage failed to meet the requirements for placement on the 2026 ballot. Florida Decides Healthcare is turning its sights to 2028.

item.title: Alan Burton, whose idea led to ReGrow the Loop, files to run for Zone 1 in Ormond Beach
item.description: Burton has lived in Ormond Beach since 1996, and is a past director of leisure services for the city.

item.title: My View: Tort reform Is working and it matters for Volusia County
item.description: Duncan DeMarsh writes: 'With the passage of House Bill 837, Florida took decisive action to rein in lawsuit abuse and restore balance to a civil justice system that had drifted far from common sense.'

item.title: Daytona Beach Area Association of Realtors celebrates renovation of Holly Hill office
item.description: The DBAAR has been serving the Daytona Beach area for 104 years, since 1922. 'Realtors are a huge part of the community,' CEO Mary Smith said. 'They touch people's lives in many different ways.'

item.title: 2026 Volusia Innovation Challenge applications open
item.description: Applicants must be at least 18 years old and live, attend school or operate a business in Volusia County. The grand prize is $10,000 cash.

item.title: 'School Board Member's Bill of Rights' legislation advances, filed after Volusia County Schools conflicts
item.description: HB 1073 and SB 1620 were created after School Board member Donna Brosemer voiced being ignored, or charged, for requesting documents from VCS, as well as budget and attorney representation concerns.

item.title: SIDELINES: FPC girls, Seabreeze boys and girls set for soccer playoffs
item.description: Also: Palm Coast Open men's singles final set for Feb. 8; LPGA Amateur Golf Association of Daytona Beach celebrates 20th anniversary.

item.title: Staying the course: Volusia County Council's 2040 vision for ECHO is to maintain status quo
item.description: The Volusia County Council examined the 2040 strategic plan for the county's ECHO program on Tuesday, Feb. 3, largely voting against implementing new recommendations.

item.title: Coastal Family Church granted appeal to continue Sunday services as lawsuit proceeds
item.description: A Flagler County court judge had approved an injunction on Jan. 25 prohibiting the church from meeting for its Sunday services. By Jan. 30, a Florida appeals court had reversed the ruling.

item.title: Flagler’s settlement offer to Hammock Harbour would allow the 240-unit dry boat storage
item.description: The offer allows Hammock Harbour to develop the site plan as-is. The county would also pay the developer $400,000 in settlement plus $150,000 in impact and building fee credits.
